findings.title: New rc3-7 SQL uses plain COALESCE(corrected, snapshot) — diverges from the established COALESCE(NULLIF(corrected,''), snapshot) convention (latent when RC4.3 writes a correction)
findings.evidence: get_application_reference_contacts.sql: COALESCE(rc.corrected_email, rc.contact_email, '') AS effective_email (no NULLIF on corrected). count_cross_application_contact_reuse.sql: COALESCE(rc.corrected_email, rc.contact_email) = NULLIF($3, '') (NULLIF on the param, not corrected). The established convention (find_reference_call_by_send_ref dedup, sql.gleam:297-298): COALESCE(NULLIF(rc.corrected_email, ''), rc.contact_email).
findings.detail: If corrected_* is ever stored as '' (not NULL), the creation SQL returns '' (losing the snapshot) while submission effective_contact(Some("")) falls back to snapshot — a divergence. Today corrected_* is always NULL (RC4.3 owns writing it and doesn't exist), so no live trigger. Comment-accuracy + consistency hardening, not merge-blocking.
findings.recommended_fix: Wrap corrected in NULLIF inside both new COALESCEs: COALESCE(NULLIF(rc.corrected_email,''), rc.contact_email, '') — matches the established convention and the effective_contact helper's documented intent. Do it when RC4.3 lands the correction write at the latest.

findings.detail: Test-only, token is test-controlled, and it follows this file's pre-existing idiom (text_column/result_field/audit_event_for/focus_seconds_reported all interpolate the same way).
